protocol.label: How long does preparing a protein-ligand complex for docking take, by hand and in Genesis
protocol.status: PREREGISTERED BEFORE ANY TIMING WAS COLLECTED FROM THE MANUAL ARM. Frozen; amendments only by append.
protocol.question: For the same ten deposited complexes and the same finish line, how much ACTIVE HUMAN TIME does preparation take by hand, and how much does it take in Genesis?
protocol.whyItExists: Genesis's own times are measured; no manual baseline exists anywhere, so no percentage saved may be claimed. This study produces that baseline. Until it is filled in, the only permitted wording remains the target '>=50% less active specialist time in the pilot workflow, to be measured'.

theTask.inputs: the ten deposited mmCIF files in docs/evidence/prep-time-study/inputs, identical for both arms
theTask.deliverablePerComplex: receptor.pdb (or .pdbqt), ligand.sdf (or .mol) with 3D coordinates and bond orders in the receptor frame, and box.json with center and size in Angstrom
theTask.method: UNPRESCRIBED. Any tools, any route. Only the result is judged.
theTask.definitionOfDone: acceptance by scripts/prep-time-study-check.py, the SAME gate for both arms; it never inspects docking results

protocol.primaryMetric: median ACTIVE human minutes per complex in the manual arm, against the active human time of the Genesis arm
secondaryMetrics: mean and full spread of active minutes per complex
the first complex reported separately from the rest, so the learning curve is visible and not hidden
waiting-on-the-computer time, reported separately and never counted as a saving
complexes the gate rejects, and complexes abandoned, in both arms
protocol.theSplitThatDecidesEverything: ACTIVE time is time a person's hands and attention are on the task. WAITING time is time a computation runs unattended. Genesis does not make a computer faster: a person running the same tools waits for their own machine too. Only active time may enter any claim about saving a specialist's time, and waiting time is reported beside it so nobody can confuse the two.

genesisArm.activeHumanTime: zero by construction - one command, then the operator is free
genesisArm.machineTimeMeasurement: reported as measured; the number that goes in the report is measured on an otherwise IDLE container, because a measurement taken while run 8 occupies all four cores would overstate it
genesisArm.provisionalMeasurement: 5.30 s total for the ten complexes, mean 0.53 s, taken 2026-09-29 while run 8 was using all four cores. Recorded here as PROVISIONAL and as an upper bound on the machine time; it is replaced by an idle-machine measurement before the report.

manualArm.operator: one person who is not the author of Genesis, working alone
manualArm.experienceIsRecordedAndReported: whether the operator has prepared a complex for docking before is recorded BEFORE the run and stated in the report. A first-timer's number measures learning the tooling, an experienced user's number measures the work, and the report says which one it is rather than passing one off as the other.
manualArm.aiAssistanceDisclosed: any AI assistance is recorded on the sheet; an undisclosed one invalidates the arm
manualArm.noCoaching: no help from Genesis, its authors or its output during the timed run

prespecifiedInterpretation.principle: The comparison is between ACTIVE human minutes in each arm. Machine time is reported but never enters the claim.
prespecifiedInterpretation.reportedAs: 'preparation took N minutes of active specialist time by hand and M seconds of unattended machine time in Genesis', with N the median and the full spread beside it
aPercentageMayBeQuotedOnlyIf: the manual arm completed at least 7 of the 10 complexes through the gate
the operator had prepared a complex for docking before this study
no undisclosed AI assistance was used
prespecifiedInterpretation.ifThoseAreNotMet: the numbers are published exactly as measured and labelled as a single operator's times, explicitly NOT a specialist baseline, and the deck wording stays the unmeasured target
prespecifiedInterpretation.nAndItsLimits: ten complexes and one operator. This is a first measurement, not a study. The report says so in its own first paragraph, and the number carries the operator's experience level with it wherever it is quoted.

forbidden: computing any percentage before the timing sheet is complete
re-running the manual arm because the first number was disappointing
dropping a complex the operator found hard
counting waiting-on-the-computer time as a saving
quoting any number from this study without the operator's experience level attached
the author of Genesis performing the manual arm
